text:
inc-bot: ALERT: p99 tail latency spike detected for router-ingress streaming paths in us-west-2. p99 ~ 7.2s (baseline 0.9s), p95 ~ 1.3s. Error rate for streaming sessions up 1.8% (normal <0.1%). Paging oncall. Please ack and start Triage. :rotating_light:

maria (oncall): Acked. seeing alerts in grafana and Kinesis stalls in tracing. Are any deploys going out?

ajay: Not seeing any deployments in the last 30m. I can see a sudden skew in routing weights to shard-12 on the ingress balancer around 15:12 UTC. Looks like the routing-policy rollout task updated prefer_local weights.

samir: Confirmed. From router logs: `route_assign: shard=12 weight=0.78 -> spike; active_conns=14k; avg_kv_miss=0.12; kv_cache_miss_p99=0.9`. We're getting hot partition behavior.

maria (oncall): Customer impact? Any major customers affected?

nisha: Quick check on downstream sessions: long-lived streaming sessions (transcription pipelines / call recording) are experiencing stalls and reconnects. I see 3 customer support tickets from large customers in last 20m referencing dropped chunks. Sending IDs privately.

kelly: Adding ops-bot note: auto-scaler attempted to add capacity but hit quota in us-west-2; scaling back failed so traffic concentrated on existing shards.

ajay: Immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback the last routing policy change (prefer_local weight rollback) 2) temporarily pin new requests away from shard-12 (weight 0) 3) enable eager-fallback to regional replicas for streaming paths. I can run (2) quickly.

maria (oncall): Do it. Also start a livebridge for oncall->sre->product. I'll open a Zoom and paste link here.

ajay: Running weight adjust now. Command:```bash
curl -X POST https://internal-router-control/api/v1/weight 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_ADMIN' 
  -d '{"shard":12,"weight":0.05,"reason":"emergency drain - usw2 hotshard"}'
```

inc-bot: ACTION TAKEN: weight change applied to shard-12 by ajay at 15:26 UTC. New weight=0.05.

samir: Pushing traffic shift metrics... p99 trending down from 7.2s -> 2.4s within 90s. p95 back to ~1.1s. Streaming stall count decreased by ~60%.

nisha: Sending customers the interim message: "We’ve routed your requests away from overloaded shard and are monitoring. Expect improved connectivity within minutes."

maria (oncall): Good. Is this safe to leave while we root-cause? We need to avoid flapping.

ajay: We should keep weight low for 30m, then investigate policy change logs. I want to roll back the prefer_local rollout on the policy agent for the last canary batch — that rollout seems to have exaggerated hotness by aggressively preferring local zones.

samir: Evidence: routing-policy agent logs show last rollout task id=rollout-2026-03-15-1510 applied incremental weight adjustments with a bug in the decay factor. Config snippet:```json
{"policy":"prefer_local","decay_factor":0.0001,"max_local_bias":0.95}``` This small decay ends up strongly biasing local weight during load spikes.

kelly: We should patch a safe cap on max_local_bias and add an emergency circuit-breaker to prevent >0.25 bias during high conn churn.

maria (oncall): Agreed. For now: keep drain, scale reserve capacity request to cloud team, and open a change rollback for the policy agent. ajay, samir, can one of you own the rollback?

ajay: I'll own the rollback. Plan: revert rollout-2026-03-15-1510 to previous stable (rollout-2026-03-14-2100), validate routing heatmap, then slowly re-apply with caps.

samir: I've started telemetry capture for shard hotness and added a high-frequency sampler to past-5m traces so we can replay and correlate KV cache miss -> tail latency. Also capturing connection churn metrics and per-region weight diffs.

ops-bot: NOTE: capacity request submitted to cloud quota team (ticket CLD-9876). Estimated 45m ETA for quota approval.

nisha: Customer impact note for postmortem: multiple long-stream sessions experienced stalls leading to at least 4 reconnect events for two enterprise tenants; downstream processing lagged 20-40s for affected sessions. No data loss confirmed.

maria (oncall): Any sign of hardware/network issues?

samir: No packet loss on infra, no host CPU saturation. This is routing imbalance + cache miss amplification.

ajay: Rollback complete at 15:44 UTC. Verified routing policy reverted. We'll keep shard-12 weight low for 20 more minutes and then gradually rebalance.

inc-bot: RESOLVED ALERT: p99 reduced to 0.98s, p95 0.95s. Streaming stalls back to baseline. Incident declared mitigated at 15:48 UTC.

maria (oncall): Great work. We'll keep monitoring for 2 hours. Please capture all patches, logs, and timeline in the incident doc.

nisha: Filed postmortem ticket PM-5123 and linked the incident notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PM-5123. I'll draft customer-facing blurb.

ajay: Follow-ups: 1) Add circuit-breaker cap to routing agent (PR opened) 2) Add hotshard early-detection alert (p99 delta > 2s + weight change >0.2 within 5m) 3) Improve scaling fallback when quota hit (fail-over to cross-region replicas).

samir: Also propose adding KV-prefetch for streaming prefix patterns to reduce cache miss amplification during spikes.

kelly: I'll coordinate with cloud to speed the quota ETA and document the runbook steps we took.

maria (oncall): Closing livebridge. Thanks everyone. Postmortem owners: nisha (writeup), ajay (policy fix), samir (telemetry), kelly (cloud ops).

inc-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigated -> monitoring).
